components: ShortLinkEndpoints: new extend routes, request validation, rate limiting, status mapping
ShortenerService: ExtendExpiry logic (owner check, state checks, cap), remainingSeconds in GetStats, audit event emission
IUrlRepository/InMemoryUrlRepository: atomic compare-and-swap update (TryReplace) so concurrent extends lose no updates
Audit logger: ILogger-based structured audit events (category UrlShortener.Audit) injected into ShortenerService via AppHost
AppHost: wiring of ILogger into ShortenerService

endpoints.summary: Owner extends expiry by additionalSeconds (FR-1, FR-2). Body {additionalSeconds}. Returns {code, expiresAt, remainingSeconds}. Expired-but-active links are revived from now.
Canonical alias of the extend operation, same handler, body and responses.
Existing stats plus additive remainingSeconds (long, null if no expiry, 0 if expired) (FR-3).
Backward-compatible alias of analytics; same response including remainingSeconds.
Metadata; reflects updated expiresAt after extend (FR-4).
Redirect unchanged; works again after extending an expired link (FR-2, FR-4).

dataModel: ShortLink record unchanged (ExpiresAt already persisted); extend creates a modified copy with new ExpiresAt via compare-and-swap.
LinkStats gains trailing nullable long RemainingSeconds (additive response field).
New ExtendExpiryRequest(long? AdditionalSeconds); ExtendExpiryResponse(Code, ExpiresAt, RemainingSeconds); ExtendStatus {Done, NotFound, Forbidden, Invalid, Deactivated, NoExpiry, TooLong}.
Audit event (log record, not persisted in store): timestamp, action=expiry.extend, code, actorHash, outcome, previousExpiresAt, newExpiresAt, additionalSeconds.
risks: Owner identity is the spoofable X-Client-Id header (existing prototype limitation); extend inherits it. Audit actor is therefore unverified.
Requirement says POST /extend, canonical list says PUT /expiry: both are exposed to satisfy both; small API surface duplication.
Audit logs may be forged via log injection or contain identifiers: log only structured fields, and a SHA-256-prefix hash of the client id, never raw header text.
Audit goes to the ILogger sink only; not tamper-proof or durable without a configured sink. Production needs an append-only store.
Overflow: huge additionalSeconds could overflow DateTimeOffset arithmetic; bound-check against the cap before adding.
CAS retry loop could spin under heavy contention; bounded retries then 409/500 are unlikely at the stated 50 concurrency.
Cap semantic (total lifetime from now <= 365 days, reusing MaxExpiryMinutes) must be tested at the boundary.
Check order (404, 403, 400, 409) leaks no extra info beyond deactivate, but an invalid body from a non-owner returns 403 first.

decisions.decision: Add audit logging for expiry changes (reviewer request): emit structured ILogger events for every extend attempt, success and denied/failed, with action, code, hashed actor, outcome, old and new expiry.
decisions.rationale: Satisfies the reviewer change request with no new infrastructure; includes denials since they are security-relevant.
decisions.alternative: Persistent audit table: more durable but needs a schema change and storage not present in the in-memory prototype.

decisions.decision: Expose both POST /api/urls/{code}/extend and PUT /api/urls/{code}/expiry on one handler.
decisions.rationale: The requirement names the former, the canonical routes name the latter; both stay consistent.
decisions.alternative: Only one route: would violate either the requirement or the canonical contract.

decisions.decision: Add IUrlRepository.TryReplace(code, expected, updated) compare-and-swap and loop in the service.
decisions.rationale: Mirrors the existing Deactivate CAS pattern; guarantees no lost updates for N concurrent extends.
decisions.alternative: A global lock: simpler but serialises all links and does not suit a future SQL repository.

decisions.decision: Compute remainingSeconds in the service from TimeProvider, floor, clamp to 0; null when ExpiresAt is null.
decisions.rationale: Deterministic with a fake clock in tests; additive and backward compatible.
decisions.alternative: Compute in the endpoint: splits logic and harder to test.

decisions.decision: Status mapping: deactivated 409, no expiry 409, bad/missing/non-positive additionalSeconds 400, cap exceeded 400, wrong owner 403 (same as deactivate), unknown 404.
decisions.rationale: Matches the acceptance criteria and the deactivate behaviour.
decisions.alternative: 422 for validation: deviates from the stated criteria.

decisions.decision: Apply FixedWindowRateLimiter to extend, keyed by client id.
decisions.rationale: Mandatory rate-limit control; reuses existing component.
decisions.alternative: No limit: leaves a mutation endpoint unthrottled.

impact.reason: Map POST /{code}/extend and PUT /{code}/expiry, handler with rate limiting, status mapping.
Add ExtendStatus/ExtendResult and RemainingSeconds on LinkStats.
Add ExtendExpiry, remainingSeconds in GetStats, audit logging.

dataFlows: Client -> POST extend (X-Client-Id, body) -> rate limiter -> body validation -> ShortenerService.ExtendExpiry -> repo.Get -> owner/state/cap checks -> repo.TryReplace (CAS, retry on conflict) -> audit log event -> 200 with new expiresAt.
Denied or failed extend (403/409/400/404) -> audit log event with outcome -> error response; no state change.
Client -> GET analytics -> service.GetStats -> repo.Get + AnalyticsStore.Get + clock -> LinkStats with remainingSeconds.
Redirect path untouched: repo.Get -> active and unexpired check -> click enqueue -> 302.
appliedChangeRequests: Add audit logging for expiry changes
